industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, with the case for Overweight stronger than at any time since the row was set and still not taken. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-11-06 against 2026-09-04, not week on week: A now, C prior: healthcare is the defensive the market is paying for, with Medtech capital goods A, Pharma/biotech B, Medtech consumables B and Pharma manufacturing services B. Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only) pays large, proven, cash-yielding cases, which is the Pharma/biotech row (B) and Hospitals (B). Held at C because the industry letter adds the same 30% weight to clinical-stage biotech (D, relative strength F) and capex-cyclical medical equipment as to large pharma, no source spoke to pharmaceuticals against medical technology this week, and eleven of the top 40 on the starting score are already healthcare names. Counter-case for B: two readings two months apart at A with the regime's rotation confirmed on every window; for D: a crowded destination. To B if a source carries a healthcare read with the industry's relative strength holding A or B.

memo.verdict: Neutral on the shares at DKK 321.4, bullish on the business. Progress as a priced watch position rather than park: progress to Early-Stage at or below about DKK 305, or sooner if the October US Veterans Affairs data and the Q3 2026 statement (early November 2026) show Zeal's Veterans Affairs share at 22 percent or more and wholesale organic growth of 8 percent or more with the gross margin held. Conviction medium: a working hypothesis on the second-half 2026 launch window, firm on the business. The park rule is not triggered (management C, business quality B, predictability B, trackability B). The record's one-line bet: that Oticon Zeal and Reveal hold wholesale share and price through the crowded second-half 2026 launch window while the cost programme, the KIND conversion and the falling debt lift the operating margin toward 19 percent, and that we pay DKK 305 or less for it. The case is a B thesis at a C price: compelling as a business change, not compelling as a return from DKK 321.4. Invalidation on the research's own reversal test: wholesale organic growth below 5 percent in Q3 or Q4 2026 with the gross margin down more than 100bp (launch window lost), or below 3 percent for two consecutive quarters; gearing above 3.8x or an acquisition before the 2.0-2.5x range is reached.
case: - Demant is a self-help recovery riding a product cycle, in the 'Major Corporate Change' pattern, compelling as a business change but not, at DKK 321.4, as a return.

- The change is internal, broad and does not depend on the market. Between mid-2025 and August 2026 four forces changed the inputs: Oticon Zeal (custom rechargeable in-the-ear) reached 23.1 percent of Veterans Affairs units at USD 695, a 42 percent premium, with two-thirds first-time wearers; Oticon Reveal launched August 2026 with net price increases expected over Intent; KIND (about 650 German clinics, DKK 5.2bn) closed December 2025 and integrates ahead of plan; a DKK 500m cost programme has DKK 300m landing in 2026 with DKK 100m delivered in H1 ahead of schedule; EPOS and Oticon Medical were sold, closing a four-year structural review with DKK 2.3bn of write-downs behind the group.

- The outputs have followed on every line: H1 2026 revenue +15 percent reported, +7 percent organic, Q2 +9 percent against consensus 6.7; all three divisions beat (wholesale +10, retail +8, diagnostics +9 percent organic); gross margin 77.1 percent, +110bp; EBIT before special items +15 percent; adjusted EPS +20 percent; gearing 3.4x to 3.0x in six months. Zeal's pull-through into the wider Oticon portfolio is reported as incremental, not cannibalising.
counter_case: - At Building Block 1: the recovery is real but it is in the price, and the second half of 2026 is where it stalls. The shares are up 67.6 percent in six months at the 99th percentile of their two-year multiple range; the guidance raise was anticipated and moved consensus about 1 percent on the day; Bernstein's downgrade of 17 July 2026 and Deutsche Bank's "limited room for re-rating" of 19 August 2026 are the sell-side form of this view, and the Holds are 9 of 17 named brokers. The FY2026 EPS step of about 20 percent is flattered by KIND's first-year consolidation and a one-off cost programme. Reveal is, on Bernstein's reading, a software update on the same Sirius chip as Intent while Sonova's EON carries a new chip and smaller housing and GN's Sensia claims the smallest AI device; four of five manufacturers launch into one window. Zeal's success is concentrated in a custom category about 10 percent of the market and a Veterans Affairs channel 5 percent of sales where prices are negotiated centrally, and about a third of candidates are excluded by ear-canal size. The independents, 52 percent of wholesale, may punish forward integration and nobody has the data. Short interest of about 10 percent of free float fuelled the 13 percent one-day rise in May 2026 and can unwind. The operator cut guidance four times in two years before raising once. The record concedes most of the facts: the re-rating has happened and none is assumed; the window cannot be seen before early November; the FY2026 step is partly inorganic and one-off; the operator is a C; the modal return is a C. It holds the view on the business (the chain is complete and broad, Zeal's category is not where the rivals land, the 2027-28 margin levers are internal and ahead of plan, the balance sheet repairs faster than the street models, OTC is disproved) and not on the price (no payment for a re-rating at 30 percent odds). Where it would win: wholesale organic growth below 5 percent in Q3 or Q4 2026 with the gross margin down more than 100bp, or Veterans Affairs Zeal share below about 20 percent for two months.

- At Building Block 2: the oligopoly's stickiness is being broken from below by the channel, and the operator cannot be trusted to steer through it. Amplifon owns a manufacturer and targets 90 percent internal supply by 2029; Costco buys at USD 200-400 against USD 300-500 for independents; the Veterans Affairs channel pays about USD 480 against up to USD 1,100 in private pay; Sam's Club, Fielmann and Specsavers are entering; wholesale price is set increasingly by buyers with scale. Demant's own forward integration is the move its research names as the largest Foundations risk, and the independents could switch supplier in exactly the window four rivals launch. Capital-allocation discipline is rated weak; software and apps lag; turnover was 20 percent after 26 percent; an untested external division leader runs Hearing Aids through the window. The record concedes the consolidation, the price-led channels, the unmeasured independent reaction, the C operator and the new president. It holds because Demant's route to market is the most diversified among the manufacturers (top 5 percent of the peer set for concentration mitigation; Amplifon-GN hurts Sonova and WS Audiology more), the premium-end attitude is margin-prioritising (intensity in product, not price), and the thesis needs competence, not more. Where it would win: external wholesale growth falling while internal sales rise, or the first discounting to defend share in the independent channel; neither is in the data yet.
triggers: - Price trigger: progress to Early-Stage at or below about DKK 305 (eighteen-month horizon, modal path); DKK 270 on the three-year horizon; about DKK 280 on the adverse drop-through path.

- Data trigger to progress sooner: October Veterans Affairs data with Zeal's share at 22 percent or more, and the Q3 2026 statement (about 5 November 2026) with wholesale organic growth of 8 percent or more and the gross margin held; both raise the odds on condition (a) and with them the odds of the 19.2x branch.

- Alarm levels: Veterans Affairs Oticon custom and total unit share below about 20 percent (two months is the signal); Zeal average selling price below about USD 600; wholesale organic growth excluding internal sales below 5 percent in Q3 or Q4 2026 with the gross margin down over 100bp (the earnings review's definitive reversal); gross margin down more than 100bp year on year; KIND contribution below DKK 300m at the FY2026 result (9 February 2027); special items more than 15 percent above DKK 400m (about DKK 460m); realised exchange-rate headwind more than 20 percent worse than DKK -125m; a cut to FY2026 guidance; a 2 percent-plus consensus EPS cut; external wholesale growth falling while internal sales rise (the signature of independents leaving); the multiple below the five-year median of 16.69x; a rival smaller premium receiver-in-canal device with demonstrable clinical superiority (reassess).
- Invalidate levels: wholesale organic growth below 3 percent for two consecutive quarters; gearing above 3.8x; an acquisition before gearing reaches 2.0-2.5x.

- Monitoring series and frequency: Veterans Affairs share and price monthly (through Bernstein and Morgan Stanley); wholesale organic growth excluding internal sales, gross margin, gearing, special items and KIND internal supply quarterly or half-yearly from the company; app-download data (Sensor Tower), Costco channel checks, the EUHA congress in October, quarterly peer prints (Sonova, GN, Amplifon, WS Audiology). Not published: independent-channel share and wholesale price by channel, the two series that would settle the second-half question; KIND same-store metrics.

- Open questions the record could not settle from the inputs: whether Reveal is more than a software update against hardware-refreshed rivals (the EUHA read and Reveal reviews); whether the independents respond to forward integration by switching supplier (no data either way); whether the interest line falls as net debt falls (the one unguided link, and the line on which the drop-through sensitivity turns); the thematic reading, pinned D on an environment-only measure with no live thematic file among the inputs; the framework's track-record and lessons files and the Wisdom Library, absent from the inputs, so repeated-error overlap was judged on three named fits; return on tangible capital, not given.
